questions.prompt: What does a cascode amplifier consist of, and what does it keep and improve compared with the CS stage?
options: Two CS stages in cascade; double the \(G_m\)
A CS device with a CG device stacked on it; same \(G_m = g_{m1}\), output resistance boosted by about \(g_mr_o\)
A follower driving a CS stage; lower output resistance
A CG device driving a CS device; lower \(G_m\)

questions.prompt: With a resistor load the cascode's gain is no better than a CS stage's. Why use it anyway?
options: It uses less supply voltage
It has lower output resistance
Its input sees little Miller multiplication, so it is faster, and with a current-source load its gain can reach about \((g_mr_o)^2\)
It has twice the \(g_m\)

The gate node, always
The bias node V_B
The output node, with \(\tau_o \approx R_DC_o\)
questions.explanation: The gate pole is small thanks to the low Miller factor, the internal node sees \(1/g_{m2}\); the output is the high-impedance node (Eq. 15.24).

A simple source would make the gain positive
